sections.sustainability: Coverage of 'The Circuit' kept building this week (Retail Gazette, WWD, edie, FashionUnited, Fibre2Fashion). Sainsbury's/Tu, M&S, New Look and Oxfam launched it with Circle-8 on 23 September to test fibre-to-fibre recycling in the UK. Phase one starts January 2027 at Oxfam's Batley site and covers automated sorting, traceability reporting and commercial models for non-reusable post-consumer textiles, which make up roughly half of the UK's ~1.4m tonnes a year. Tu's A/W26 range also includes its first recycled down-and-feather puffer (£85).
sections.strategy: Tu is still pushing premiumisation with its A/W26 womenswear, which Sainsbury's calls its 'most elevated' yet, led by Head of Womenswear Buying Mel Evans. Premium knitwear options are up fourfold (cashmere, mohair and alpaca join merino and lambswool), and outerwear is the lead category. The context is softer trading: Q1 FY26/27 Tu sales fell 2.1% against a tough comparison, after FY25/26 grew 4.8%. The spring buying/merchandising restructure has still not been publicly concluded.
sections.pricing: Tu keeps an 'accessible premium' price structure. 86% of A/W26 womenswear is under £30 and 65% under £25, with entry prices from £5. Premium fibres start at £34 (lambswool), £45 (mohair) and £69 (cashmere), and hero outerwear sits at £55–£85. Back-to-school prices were held flat for a fourth year running, so value anchors stay intact against Primark, George and F&F.
sections.launches: The phased A/W26 womenswear drops continue. September's warm neutrals and orange/brown edit is in store now. October brings green shades, frogging details and the main coat launch, then November brings red, statement florals and embellished occasionwear, with more product in December. The Christmas gifting and partywear hub is live on tu.co.uk, and the Morris & Co collaboration continues.
sections.gossip: Trade press still frames Tu as a supermarket brand trying to reset perceptions of 'supermarket fashion'. Attention is now on whether premiumisation can reverse the Q1 sales dip. The next hard data point is Sainsbury's interim results (28 weeks to mid-September), expected in early November.
soWhat: The October coat launch and the fourfold premium knitwear expansion mean current-season demand for wool-blend, double-faced and premium natural-fibre fabrics. Suppliers with lambswool, mohair or cashmere-blend capability should be pitching for SS27/AW27 repeats now, while the buying team is in expansion mode.

The Circuit (from January 2027) and Tu's first recycled-down puffer show recycled-content and traceability credentials becoming commercial differentiators at Tu. Get GRS/RCS documentation and fibre-origin traceability ready before the next range reviews.

Q1's 2.1% sales dip, the unresolved buying/merchandising restructure and flat headline price points point to tight cost negotiations. Expect margin pressure on basics even as premium lines grow, and prepare cost-engineering options ahead of the early-November interims.
